subject: history
title: Revolutions: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the language of revolutions and the three biggest of the modern era.
meta_desc: GCSE History Revolutions foundations — American, French and Russian revolutions vocab.
final_note: You learned the core vocabulary and key dates of the three big revolutions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thirteen British colonies in North America rebelled over taxes and 'no taxation without representation'.

The Declaration of Independence in 1776 proclaimed a free republic. With French help, the colonies won independence by 1783.

France was bankrupt and unequal. The Estates-General met in 1789. On 14 July 1789 Parisians stormed the Bastille prison.

King Louis XVI was executed in January 1793. Then came the Reign of Terror and finally Napoleon.

WWI brought hunger and defeat. In February 1917, strikes forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate.

In October 1917 the Bolsheviks, led by Lenin, seized power. They made peace with Germany and built the world's first communist state.

mcqs.q: What happened in the Russian Revolution of 1917?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.
There were two revolutions: February overthrew the Tsar and installed the Provisional Government; October saw the Bolsheviks seize power from that government.
The Bolsheviks overthrew the Tsar in 1917.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Lenin personally led the storming of the Winter Palace.
Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.

mcqs.q: Why was the NHS founded in 1948?
options: The NHS was founded in 1918 after the influenza pandemic.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Beveridge's 1942 report identified disease as a 'giant evil'; Labour's 1945 manifesto promised universal healthcare; Bevan unified hospitals and made care free at point of use.
The NHS was founded because Churchill wanted to thank soldiers after WWII.
